arxiv-2109-06730.title: A Hierarchical Control Framework for Drift Maneuvering of Autonomous Vehicles
arxiv-2109-06730.creator: Bo Yang, Yiwen Lu, Xu Yang, Yilin Mo
arxiv-2109-06730.description: Abstract Maneuvering an autonomous vehicle under drift condition is critical to the safety of autonomous vehicles when there is a sudden loss of traction due to external conditions such as rain or snow, which is a challenging control problem due to the presence of significant sideslip and nearly full saturation of the tires.

arxiv-2209-06768.title: Multi-band character revealed from Weak-antilocalization effect in Platinum thin films
arxiv-2209-06768.creator: Subhadip Jana, T. Senapati, K. Senapati, D. Samal
arxiv-2209-06768.description: Abstract Platinum (Pt) has been very much used for spin-charge conversion in spintronics research due to it’s large intrinsic spin-orbit interaction. Magnetoconductance originated from weak-antilocalization effect in quantum interference regime is used as a powerful tool to obtain the microscopic information of spin-orbit interaction and coherence phase breaking scattering process among itinerant electrons.

arxiv-2312-09089.title: On-Chip Multidimensional Dynamic Control of Twisted Moiré Photonic Crystal for Smart Sensing and Imaging
arxiv-2312-09089.creator: Haoning Tang ⊥, Beicheng Lou ⊥, Fan Du, Guangqi Gao, Mingjie Zhang, Xueqi Ni, Evelyn Hu, Amir Yacoby, Yuan Cao, Shanhui Fan, Eric Mazur
arxiv-2312-09089.description: Abstract $\bot$ $\bot$ footnotetext: These authors contributed equally to this work Reconfigurable optics, optical systems that have a dynamically tunable configuration, are emerging as a new frontier in photonics research. Recently, twisted moiré photonic crystal has become a competitive candidate for implementing reconfigurable optics because of its high degree of tunability.

arxiv-2406-02332.title: Extended Mind Transformers
arxiv-2406-02332.creator: Phoebe Klett, Thomas Ahle
arxiv-2406-02332.description: Abstract Pre-trained language models demonstrate general intelligence and common sense, but long inputs quickly become a bottleneck for memorizing information at inference time. We resurface a simple method, Memorizing Transformers (Wu et al., 2022), that gives the model access to a bank of pre-computed memories.

arxiv-2406-03784.title: Constructing tree amplitudes of scalar EFT from double soft theorem
arxiv-2406-03784.creator: Kang Zhou
arxiv-2406-03784.description: Abstract The well known Adler zero can fully determine tree amplitudes of non-linear sigma model (NLSM), but fails to fix tree pion amplitudes with higher-derivative interactions. To fill this gap, in this paper we propose a new method based on exploiting the double soft theorem for scalars, which can be applied to a wider range.

arxiv-2505-02671.title: Characterisation of Crystalline Defects in 4H Silicon Carbide using DLTS and TSC
arxiv-2505-02671.creator: Moritz Wiehe
arxiv-2505-02671.description: Abstract Future hadron collider experiments will require sensing materials that withstand stronger radiation fields. Therefore, either a frequent replacement of detectors, a significant increase in radiation hardness of Silicon, or a shift to different materials is needed. Wide-bandgap materials are a natural choice, due to their significantly reduced leakage currents, even after irradiation.

britannica-1911-shropshire.description: Article 'Shropshire' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 24), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Geology.—The Pre-Cambrian rocks of Shropshire include the granitoid and gneissic rocks of the Ercall and Primrose Hill (Wrekin), the schists of Rushton, the lavas and ashes of the Wrekin, Caer Caradoc and Pontesford, and the purple slates, grits and conglomerates of the Longmynd. The Wrekin Quartzite, Comley Sandstone and Shineton Shales are the local representatives of the Cambrian system.

pmc-11393062.title: Consensus of algorithms for lesion segmentation in brain MRI studies of multiple sclerosis
pmc-11393062.creator: Alessandro Pasquale De Rosa, Marco Benedetto, Stefano Tagliaferri, Francesco Bardozzo, Alessandro D’Ambrosio, Alvino Bisecco, Antonio Gallo, Mario Cirillo, Roberto Tagliaferri, Fabrizio Esposito
pmc-11393062.description: Segmentation of multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions on brain MRI scans is crucial for diagnosis, disease and treatment monitoring but is a time-consuming task. Despite several automated algorithms have been proposed, there is still no consensus on the most effective method. Here, we applied a consensus-based framework to improve lesion segmentation on T1-weighted and FLAIR scans.

pmc-11596618.title: Food Webs and Feedbacks: The Untold Ecological Relevance of Antimicrobial Resistance as Seen in Harmful Algal Blooms
pmc-11596618.creator: Aabir Banerji, Nichole E Brinkman, Benjamin Davis, Alison Franklin, Michael Jahne, Scott P Keely, Burkhard Becker
pmc-11596618.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has long been framed as an epidemiological and public health concern. Its impacts on the environment are unclear. Yet, the basis for AMR is altered cell physiology. Just as this affects how microbes interact with antimicrobials, it can also affect how they interact with their own species, other species, and their non-living environment.

pmc-12578316.title: Novel amino acid residues in listerolysin O drive phagosome escape and pathogenicity in Listeria monocytogenes
pmc-12578316.creator: Jing Xia, Yuchao Feng, Jiali Xu, Simin Deng, Mianmian Chen, Yue Han, Jing Wang, Jing Sun, Kalliopi Rantsiou, Luca Simone Cocolin, Houhui Song, Changyong Cheng
pmc-12578316.description: Listeria monocytogenes, a significant zoonotic foodborne intracellular pathogen, relies on its principal virulence factor, listeriolysin O (LLO), to escape from host cell phagosomes-a critical step for establishing intracellular infection and replication. LLO, composed of four structural domains with amino acids essential for its pore-forming abilities, still harbors many sites with undefined roles.

pmc-12612645.title: An mHealth App and System Architecture for Respiratory Disease Management: Design Principles, Tool Development, and Pilot Usability Study
pmc-12612645.creator: Andrew Chao, Lisa Martignetti, René Groh, Andreas M Kist, Nicole YK Li-Jessen
pmc-12612645.description: BackgroundMobile health (mHealth) apps are software interfaces that enable users to access and manage wearable technology through smartphones and tablet devices for health improvement purposes. However, many respiratory disease mHealth apps lack transparent development documentation, compromising user confidence in their quality, functionality, and usability.

pmc-13187298.title: Three-dimensional ex-vivo visualization of normal and inflamed small intestine and colonic tissue using optical coherence tomography
pmc-13187298.creator: Abigail Matt, Yilin Li, Andrew Song, Billy D. Nix, Katherine Huang, Umang Jain, Changqing Ma, Chao Zhou, Parakkal Deepak
pmc-13187298.description: Inflammatory bowel diseases, including Crohn’s Disease (CD) and Ulcerative Colitis (UC), are characterized by inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. Early diagnoses are critical in the determination of an effective treatment. Current methods of tissue assessment remain two-dimensional and limited by lack of information under the surface of the mucosal layer.

pmc-13377031.title: RESPECT: a conversational AI system for informed consent with accuracy, safety, and stakeholder-centered evaluation
pmc-13377031.creator: Salvatore Giorgi, Katie Ryan, Jane Paik Kim
pmc-13377031.description: Informed consent (IC) is a cornerstone of clinical research. IC typically includes both written materials and, particularly in clinical trials, an oral discussion between the investigator and participant. In practice, both components tend to be templated and standardized, limiting opportunities for meaningful, individualized dialog.

pmc-13390245.title: Quantitative genetic analyses of traits related to calcium and phosphorus metabolism in two different laying hen strains
pmc-13390245.creator: Valentin P Haas, Markus Schmid, Vera Sommerfeld, Amélia Camarinha-Silva, Martina Feger, Michael Föller, Korinna Huber, Michael Oster, Siriluck Ponsuksili, Jana Seifert, Klaus Wimmers, Jörn Bennewitz, Markus Rodehutscord
pmc-13390245.description: BackgroundPhosphorus (P) and calcium (Ca) are essential minerals for laying hens. Phosphorus in plant feeds is mainly stored as phytate and needs to be released by the enzyme phytase. Due to the high requirement of Ca, laying hens exhibit limited endogenous phytate degradation and thus plant-P is available to a limited extent.

pmc-13454172.title: Remnant cholesterol is independently associated with liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease patients and rats
pmc-13454172.creator: Ruifang Li, Rong Ren, Guifeng Li, Ping Han, Lili Zhao, Jia Li
pmc-13454172.description: Few studies have explored the relationship between remnant cholesterol (RC) and liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD). Therefore, this study aims to explore the association between RC levels and liver fibrosis in both biopsy-proven MAFLD population and Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats. This current study included 280 participants and 15 SD rats.
